taxi.tip.detour-normal.title: A diversion is not necessarily a scam
taxi.tip.detour-normal.body: Traffic, closures and tunnel queues all cause re-routing. The fare may be a little higher and still be legitimate.
taxi.tip.meter-on.title: The meter must be running
taxi.tip.meter-on.body: Fares follow the official scale — they are not negotiated. If the meter isn't on, just say 「唔該，用咪錶」.
taxi.tip.receipt-right.title: You have a right to a receipt
taxi.tip.receipt-right.body: It shows the fare and the taxi's details, which is what makes a later complaint possible. Ask before you pay.
taxi.tip.extras-on-top.title: Surcharges sit outside the meter
taxi.tip.extras-on-top.body: Tunnel tolls, luggage and pets carry defined surcharges, so the total exceeding the meter is normal.
taxi.tip.refusal.title: Refusing a hire can be reported
taxi.tip.refusal.body: Note the plate and the driver's licence number and take it to the Transport Department — no need to argue at the kerb.
taxi.tip.note-details.title: Note the taxi's details first
taxi.tip.note-details.body: The plate and driver's licence number are displayed inside. With those and a receipt a complaint can be followed up.
taxi.title: Taking a taxi
taxi.estimateNote: The estimate excludes luggage and pet surcharges. The meter is what counts.
taxi.tariffNote: Fares follow the Transport Department scale

taxi.plateNotedSub: With a receipt this is what a Transport Department complaint needs
taxi.receiptWhy: A receipt shows the fare and the plate — you need it to complain.
taxi.notLegalAdvice: General information, not legal advice. See td.gov.hk for current rules.
